title: Racking a server
alt: A side section through an open server rack, 600 by 1200 mm, half full, with its mesh front door swung open and a rail at every slot. Beside it stands a cart of new servers. A technician lifts a server off the cart with both hands and slides it along the rails into the rack, the server moving with her hands and fitting fully inside the frame. A second technician holds the next server ready, and it goes in the same way. The full rack is fed by a power drop at the back.
sources: Rack size 600 x 1200 mm: Vertiv VR3300 (maker data)
About 7 to 8 kW per rack on average: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2024, p. 10 (industry survey)
drawn_generically: technicians are plain white figures, 1.75 m, with arms reaching forward; servers drawn as 2 rack units, generic
the cart stands beside the rack, drawn lighter behind the people
camera: the rack and cart, closer for the slide, then the full rack

steps.caption: A rack in the data hall, half full, with its front door open. Beside it, a cart of new servers.
A technician lifts a server off the cart with both hands.
She slides it into the rails, pushing it all the way in.
A second technician holds the next server ready.
Slot by slot the rack fills, each server fully inside the frame.
A full rack draws about 7 to 8 kW on average, through the power drop at the back.
